idiom_name: RenderFragment<TItem> template parameters on a behaviour-owning component
implementation_notes: Blazor's templated components are the framework's realization of the pattern: the component receives one or more UI templates as parameters - RenderFragment and RenderFragment<TValue> - and uses them inside its own rendering logic, so the component owns state and behaviour while the call site supplies the markup, including a per-item template the component invokes with its data. What replaces prop getters is the component's own parameters plus the framework's re-render: the call site passes markup, not attribute bags. Keep the invariant (what is active, what is expanded) in the component's code and render only through the supplied templates.
pitfalls: A RenderFragment parameter the call site forgets compiles and renders nothing: mark it EditorRequired or throw in OnParametersSet when it is null.
Templates are invoked on every render, so expensive content should be keyed (@key) or the component should avoid re-rendering its whole tree; a fresh lambda each render defeats diffing.
Cascading state is a separate mechanism: a templated component that also cascades state makes the contract implicit and can attach children to the wrong ancestor.

variants.name: WPF: ControlTemplate and ContentPresenter separate look from behaviour
variants.implementation_notes: WPF realizes the same split in XAML: the ControlTemplate defines the appearance of a control whose behaviour lives in the control class ('the template connects the visual presentation of the control with the control's capabilities'), TemplateBinding exposes control properties to the template, and a ContentPresenter inside a ContentControl renders whatever Content/ContentTemplate the consumer supplied - the consumer literally supplies the visual tree while the control keeps the behaviour. Choose this variant in XAML codebases; when behaviour must also be shared, put it in a service or an attached behaviour, because templates carry no logic.
variants.code_sketch:
<ControlTemplate TargetType="{x:Type local:Disclosure}">   <!-- consumer's markup -->
    <Border Background="{TemplateBinding Background}">
        <StackPanel>
            <ToggleButton IsChecked="{Binding IsExpanded,
                            RelativeSource={RelativeSource TemplatedParent}}"/>
            <ContentPresenter Content="{TemplateBinding Content}"/>
        </StackPanel>
    </Border>
</ControlTemplate>
pitfalls: Changing the visual tree means replacing the whole ControlTemplate - there is no partial replacement - so consumers must start from a full template.
Template parts looked up by name (PART_*) must exist or the control's behaviour silently degrades: document the parts and assert them in OnApplyTemplate.
TemplateBinding is one-way and optimized for template use; two-way state (an expanded toggle) needs a regular Binding to the templated parent.
